submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires on the token that completes a locally predictable two-part chunk: the second subword of a word, the second word of a fixed collocation or function-word phrase (e.g. central bank, second half, According to, pinch of), or a continuation inside a digit or symbolic sequence. Strength is set jointly by the preceding token and the peak token, so the same peak token fires weakly when its chunk partner is replaced.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Day 214 of the harbor restoration project began with fog over the northern piers. Crews from district nine assembled near the customs house before sunrise, hauling cables, lanterns, and crates of rivets across the wet cobblestones. Foreman Okafor assigned teams to dredge the silted channel while divers inspected the cracked pilings beneath pier four. Gulls circled the lighthouse as tugboats guided a grain barge toward the eastern locks. By midmorning the fog lifted, revealing scaffolding along the warehouse roofs and painters sanding the old ferry terminal. A messenger arrived with revised tide charts and a request for extra pumps at the dry dock. Engineers debated whether the seawall foundations would hold through the winter storms. Lunch was served in the mess tent: barley soup, pickled herring, and dark rye bread. Afterward the survey crew mapped erosion near the salt marshes with drones and ranging poles. Dockworkers unloaded timber from Bergen, copper ingots from Lisbon, and wool bales bound for the inland mills. The harbor master logged each shipment in triplicate, stamping manifests with the brass seal of the port authority. Rumors spread that the prime minister toured the harbor districts due to flooding complaints from coastal voters last spring. Inspectors photographed hull HX-4419 in dry dock three, noting rust along the keel and barnacles near the rudder post. Welders repaired the trawler Seabird while riggers replaced frayed mooring lines on the clipper Aurora. Children from the hillside school watched the cranes swing containers onto flatbed wagons. At dusk the tide turned, and lanterns along the quay flickered on one by one. Night watchmen patrolled the warehouses with dogs, checking locks and shuttered windows. A violin quartet played in the officers club while clerks tallied the day's tonnage by candlelight. Far offshore a storm gathered, and radio operators warned incoming vessels to anchor beyond the breakwater until dawn.
